question: Should fal Compute become a built-in Crabbox provider, and must https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/693 complete a funded create, SSH/use, destroy, and zero-residue run before merge?
rationale: The adapter direction fits repository architecture, but adding a built-in paid-resource provider and accepting lifecycle safety without a successful funded run require maintainer ownership rather than automated triage judgment.

options.title: Require funded lifecycle proof
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open until the exact refreshed head completes create, SSH/use, destroy, and verified zero-residue proof with redacted output.

options.title: Waive the funded gate
options.body: Approve the built-in provider based on contract tests and authenticated read-only proof, while explicitly accepting that the first funded lifecycle remains unverified.

options.title: Decline built-in support
options.body: Close the implementation direction and leave fal integration outside Crabbox until product priorities or provider access change.

recommendation.title: Require funded lifecycle proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue and PR open until the exact refreshed head completes create, SSH/use, destroy, and verified zero-residue proof with redacted output.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked PR identifies maintainer-side integration work, making this the strongest available owner for the built-in-provider and proof-gate decision.
